questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To experiance a new culture and meet international people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great experiance!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. They had an opening session with a lot of information and also send decent information on e-mail

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A powerpoint slide with important information

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I thought everything worked fine

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in a student residence. Worked very well. However it was a bit far away from the university, but even that you get used to in my experiance. Don't choose to live right next to the university, because that area is not very interesting in my opinion

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do whatever you prefer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As I found housing on my own I didn't really explore what was made avaliable to students

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Before going I had to call them a couple of times to make sure that I had understood everything correctly, but in general it was pretty easy to navigate

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You signed up for courses online from home and then you had a period after classes had begun (about 1-2 weeks) in which you could change your courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office at the campus was open most days, so you could always just go and ask

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not a lot of advice as things worked out pretty smoothly for me and everyone I know

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses are very different from those at KU, but it was nice to experiance a different way of doing things for one semester

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most courses where not very academically challenging, but not a waste of time either

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was completely different. It was mostly smaller classes and generally some more interaction between students and professors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European Integration
International Taxation
International Economics
Public Treasury
Objectives and Instruments of Economic Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Might have been particular to my experiance, but the vibe in the European Integration classes were really cool. Very interactive, lots of international students and a very friendly atmosphere. Also the topics were quite interesting for the most part

Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No major ones. The costs I had I did kinda expect. Btw. the numbers above may not be too accurate since I haven't kept close track of my exact expenses but tried to just spend my money wisely but without holding back too much

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was less expensive than I thought

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They seemed to be quite good, but I didn't really explore them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The had some football tournaments, sports classes etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like football, I would definitely download the CeleBreak app. Gave me a bunch of good experiances. Daytrips are nice and especially Girona I would recommend. Then just enjoy life in the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Girona, Madrid and Costa Brava

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open. Talk to people on the opening session, hook up on whatapp and ask them if they wanna meet up and do something

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Didn't have to much to do with the locals, but of course when you meet international people there are some differences in culture e.g. people are more inclined to be late down south in Europe. However, they cultural differences was one of the most refreshing parts

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everything is so chill. In general people are there to meet new people and enjoy their time which reflects in the culture. Here I'm not talking only about the culture of Barcelona but also about the culture amongst Erasmus students

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, write people and ask them to do stuff, try to meet people from different cultures

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, just be attentive to the information you receive and contact either KU and UB if you have any doubts

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships with people from other countries and personal growth

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning when you still don't know how things are going to pan out. Also being very intensely together with people you barely know and from different countries can also be challenging, but in the end it is also rewarding

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would really recommend going. Had a great experiance

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
